If you are fascinated by the future where AI evolves from tools into true partners, we warmly invite you to join the Microsoft Research Asia StarTrack Scholars Program. Building on this strategic vision, Microsoft Research Asia has been actively turning the Agentic AI framework into reality through concrete, large-scale collaborative projects. With contributions from more than ten people, including Microsoft FTEs and interns, the project exemplifies the spirit of collaborative research in agentic AI, integrating expertise across LLM reasoning, reinforcement learning, data synthesis, and large-scale system design. While InfoAgent demonstrates the power of large-scale collaborative engineering in autonomous deep research, the StarTrack Scholars Program equally emphasizes nurturing exceptional individual researchers who bring fresh ideas and drive targeted breakthroughs within the Agentic AI ecosystem. ### Microsoft Research Asia StarTrack Scholars 2026: Crafting Spatial and Embodied Foundation Models for AI.

results.content: # Agentic AI In 2026: Four Predictions For Business Leaders. A late 2025 McKinsey report found that 62% of organizations are experimenting with agentic AI, with 23% beginning to scale agents in at least one business function. The important questions for leaders as we enter a new stage of agentic AI are: What does it look like to work alongside AI agents? ## Four Predictions for Agentic AI in 2026. Today, organizations are largely still in the experimentation stage with agentic AI. Eventually, agentic AI may require a single leader to oversee governance and security of all data. Organizations that win will treat agentic AI like core infrastructure. AI agents will become a new class of “intellectual worker,” requiring new human oversight skills. Machine identity security will be the No. 1 blind spot for agentic AI adoption. As agentic AI accelerates, these digital identities will become the way agents access systems, move data and make decisions.
